I opened all six papers and read around every quotation. The numbers and summaries are almost uniformly sound — but the **critique** paragraphs contain exactly the R9 failure specs.md warns about.

**Two blocking:**

- **D1.1 — Lottery Scheduling (PDF p. 8).** The answer argues the authors retreat to long time intervals and so concede the millisecond-to-second timescale. The sentence *immediately after* the 19.08:1 figure is "…we should also examine its behavior over shorter time intervals", followed by Figure 5 and the claim that a 10 ms quantum would give "the same degree of fairness … over a series of subsecond time windows". The criticism is aimed at a retreat that does not happen. Also, "individual 60-second runs scatter badly" is contradicted by the clause the 13.42:1 number was lifted from.
- **D1.2 — Buttazzo (PDF p. 10).** "…yet the abstract and conclusions generalise anyway." They do not — the quoted sentence continues "but just confutes the common belief…", and the conclusion says RM's properties "do not hold in general" and that *both* algorithms are "not very well suited" to jitter control. The answer's own later paragraph quotes that hedge as evidence Buttazzo "does not stack the deck", so it refutes itself.

Seven minor items are recorded but are not why this fails.
